Программа включает четыре очных модуля, последний из которых запланирован на апрель 2026 года.</p><p>Ранее четверо финалистов получили мандаты по итогам выборов в муниципальные собрания Московской области, некоторые проходят стажировку в региональных министерствах. </p><p>Один из участников, Кирилл Лосунчуков, назначен заместителем министра инвестиций, промышленности и науки Подмосковья.</p><p>По завершении обучения лучшие выпускники смогут войти в кадровый резерв или получить предложения о трудоустройстве.</p>

title: В Подмосковье открылся VI Съезд педиатров с участием специалистов из 28 стран
description: <p>По данным пресс-службы губернатора и правительства Подмосковья, в мероприятии принимают участие специалисты из 75 регионов России и 28 стран. Проведение съезда соответствует задачам федерального проекта &#171;Охрана материнства и детства&#187; нацпроекта &#171;Семья&#187;.</p><p>Губернатор региона Андрей Воробьев, открывая съезд, отметил важность обмена опытом между специалистами. </p><p class="article__quote">&#171;Смысл нашего съезда &#8211; собрать лучших профессионалов для совершенствования медицинской помощи детям. Останавливаться недопустимо, особенно когда речь идет о самом дорогом&#187;, </p><p>&#8212; заявил Воробьев.</p><p>В рамках мероприятия представлены новейшие технологии в педиатрии, включая разработки Детского клинического центра им. Рошаля, где проведено уже более 16 тысяч операций.</p><p class="article__quote">&#171;Я очень благодарен за приглашение прийти сюда, посмотреть, как живет наше здравоохранение. Уже несколько лет делаю это и получаю огромное удовольствие. Потом делюсь полученными впечатлениями в своем Бакулевском центре, где многие удивляются уровнем развития медицины в регионе", </p><p>&#8211; сказал президент Национального медицинского исследовательского центра сердечно-сосудистой хирургии им. А.Н. Бакулева Лео Бокерия.</p><p>Особое внимание также уделено проекту &#171;Наш участковый врач&#187;, который реализуется в 44 регионах России.</p><p>Съезд продлится до 5 сентября и включит симпозиумы с экспертами из США, ОАЭ, Турции и других стран, а также специализированные форумы по диетологии, реабилитации и орфанным заболеваниям.</p><p>Ранее власти Подмосковья сообщили о том, что с начала 2025 года уже около 900 тысяч детей прошли бесплатные медицинские осмотры.</p>

title: Губернатор Московской области посетил Технолицей им. Долгих в День знаний
description:
<p>По данным властей Подмосковья, в новом учебном году в этом образовательном учреждении будут обучаться 1083 студента, включая 72 первоклассника и 28 выпускников.</p><p class="article__quote">&#171;Самые смелые мечты, самые большие высоты, которые вы хотите взять, пусть покоряются. Мы будем с вами, мы в вас верим, любим вас, только вперед&#187;, </p><p>&#8211; обратился к лицеистам губернатор Московской области Андрей Воробьев. Он также отметил, что в этом году в регионе в школу пойдут порядка 1,1 млн учеников.
</p><p>Технолицей, созданный в соответствии с задачами национального проекта "Молодежь и дети", является одним из трех флагманских образовательных кластеров Подмосковья. 
</p><p>Учреждение специализируется на технологическом и естественно-научном профилях. Оно сотрудничает с ведущими техническими вузами всей России.
</p><p>Особенностью лицея является билингвальная образовательная среда с изучением китайского языка и углубленной программой по робототехнике, программированию и технологиям беспилотных аппаратов. Как следует из сообщения властей Подмосковья, педагогический коллектив насчитывает 122 преподавателя из 14 стран и 39 регионов России.
</p><p>В мае 2025 года на базе лицея создан Региональный математический центр &#171;Вектор&#187;, координирующий работу более 2000 математических классов в области.
</p><p>Ранее Андрей Воробьев заявил о том, что на базе Технолицея открыли два кампуса для проживания иногородних учащихся.</p>

title: Ed Sheeran calls Gaza war catastrophic after dropping Macklemore over pro-Palestinian comments
description: English singer Ed Sheeran opened his first show since his opener Macklemore was dropped after making pro-Palestinian comments onstage. The move sparked controversy and prompted several other support acts to drop out of the tour, publishing statements citing their support for Palestinians. While some concert goers could be seen trying to sell their tickets on Saturday, others have voiced their support for the 'Shape of You' singer. Story by Charlotte Hughes.

title: Three media outlets barred from the White House over 'fake news'
description: Donald Trump has suggested that more news outlets may be barred from the White House after he announced he was banning Politico, CNN and MS NOW. On Saturday, all three outlets said that the White House confiscated their teams' press passes; they have also hinted at legal action. The ban has come under sharp criticism from press freedom advocates, as Charlotte Hughes explains.

title: US and Denmark reach Greenland security deal
description: The US and Denmark have announced a deal on Greenland's security, resolving a diplomatic dispute sparked by President Donald Trump when he threatened to seize the semi-autonomous territory. The exact terms of the deal remain uncertain but it seems Denmark will maintain its sovereignty while the US will be able to develop a significant military presence on the island, and ban their adversaries from building their own bases on the island. Details by Charlotte Hughes.

title: Yemen's Houthis strike Saudi capital Riyadh for the first time
description: Fighting between Iran-backed Houthi rebels and Saudi Arabia continues to intensify. On Saturday morning, a fire broke out near Riyadh's main airport after Houthis said they launched missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia. On the ground in Yemen, Houthi rebels are pushing east in their fight against Saudi-backed government forces. Story by Caroline Baum.

title: Argentines protest Milei's austerity, demanding higher wages and public spending
description: Tensions are boiling over in Argentina, where a massive wave of public anger is spilling onto the streets of the capital. Following months of aggressive economic reforms and rising household debt, hundreds took to the streets in a "March of Anger", targeting President Javier Milei's austerity agenda. Details by Caitlin Brown.

title: Will German's far right party AfD win over two more regions?
description: Two weeks after the far-right AfD won its first major regional election in Germany, two more eastern states vote this Sunday. Polls have just opened in the capital, Berlin, and the largely rural state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Berlin, Jörg Taszman.

description: Paris Saint-Germain will travel to Marseille this Sunday to face OM at the Vélodrome in the final game of Matchday 5 in Ligue 1. It is a must-not-lose clash between two struggling sides, both looking to use this huge fixture to kick-start their seasons.

Live: Russian election enters final day after Kyiv targets Moscow in massive drone attack
description: Ukraine launched what Moscow’s Mayor Sergei Sobyanin described on Sunday as the “largest ever” attack on the Russian capital, killing two people and damaging part of an oil refinery. The major attack comes on the third and final day of voting in Russia’s first wartime parliamentary election. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

title: Merz under pressure as two more German states hold elections
description: Germans began voting Sunday in two closely watched state elections that could deliver fresh gains for the far-right and far-left, piling pressure on Chancellor Friedrich Merz as he struggles with low approval ratings and tensions within his governing coalition.

title: <![CDATA[Pop, Protests & Palestine: Ed Sheeran’s Moral Maze]]>
description: A clash over music, politics and Palestine is putting freedom of expression in the spotlight. Macklemore’s outspoken support for Palestinians has sparked a backlash around Ed Sheeran’s US tour, raising a bigger question: should artists be expected to take a political stand, or are they equally free to stay silent? France 24’s Gavin Lee is joined by Dr Adam Behr, Reader in Music, Politics and Society at Newcastle University, to discuss the controversy.

title: French police arrest two Germans after 'for fun' Louvre stunt in Mona Lisa hall
description: Two Germans were arrested Saturday after they stuck two paintings on a wall of the hall that hosts the Mona Lisa in Paris's Louvre Museum, police sources said.

The visit comes weeks after US President Donald Trump posted an image on social media showing the archipelago covered by the American flag.

description: White House correspondents for CNN, MS NOW and Politico on Saturday were blocked from entering the US president's office and residence a day after President Donald Trump announced he was banning the three media outlets for what he called "fake news" coverage. News organisations and press freedom groups have slammed the move as unconstitutional.

title: Germany braces for key state elections where far right party AfD seeks another breakthrough
description: Germany is gearing up for two more pivotal state elections on Sunday: in the capital Berlin and in the largely rural region of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. All eyes are on the far-right AfD, which after recording its best ever result in the recent Saxony-Anhalt elections, is hoping to once again make sweeping gains. The anti-immigration party's surging popularity is proving challenging for Chancellor Friedrich Merz and both elections are expected to further test his leadership. Story by Eliza Herbert.

title: Macron visits remote French territory in the North America, a first in over a decade
description: President Emmanuel Macron embarks on a rare and symbolic visit to a remote French territory in the North Atlantic on Saturday, hosting Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney at a time of growing tensions with Washington. The three-day visit to Saint Pierre and Miquelon, a three-island archipelago of under 6,000 people just off Newfoundland, will be the first by a French president in over a decade. Peter O'Brien tells us more about France's only remaining possession in North America.

title: Black smoke seen near Riyadh amid air raid alerts in Saudi Arabia
description: ⁠Flames and plumes of smoke ‌were ⁠seen ‌rising near ⁠Riyadh airport this afternoon with flights cancelled and delayed. This as fighting between Saudi-backed government forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels has killed 48 people in recent hours. The rebels staged a lightning offensive this month, seizing swathes of territory in Yemen and launching a barrage of missiles and drones toward Saudi Arabia. Details and analysis by FRANCE 24 international affairs editor, Jamie Smith-Maillet.

title: As petrol prices rise, France turns to bioethanol – a cheaper fuel alternative
description: With the prices of fuel continuously escalating, more and more drivers have been switching to bioethanol in France. It's cheaper to produce and currently costs around 95 cents per liter. Details by Shirli Sitbon.

title: China is now Rwanda’s biggest export market – now comes the hard part
description: In the first quarter of 2026, China became the leading destination for Rwandan exports, accounting for 26% of the total, compared with less than 5% just one year earlier. A spectacular shift, driven by the removal of Chinese tariffs on almost all Rwandan products. But on the ground, access to this market of 1.4 billion consumers depends less on tariffs than on meeting sanitary standards. Report by Aurore Bayoud.

title: France's Macron hosts Canadian PM Carney amid US tensions
description: President Emmanuel Macron embarks on a rare and symbolic visit to a remote French territory in the North Atlantic on Saturday, hosting Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney at a time of growing tensions with Washington. This comes after European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed making Canada the EU’s first associate member. Analysis by Guillaume Lavoie, associate member of the Raoul-Dandurand chair in strategic and diplomatic studies.

title: Putin says Europe is 'preparing for war'
description: As the West continues to denounce Russian aggression in Ukraine and to support Kyiv with a host of economic and military measures, Russian President Vladimir Putin says that Nato is expanding its reach and influence with the intention of preparing for war with Russia. Analysis by Dr Alexander Titov, lecturer in Modern European History at Queen's University Belfast in the UK.

title: Millions without power in Cuba as electrical grid collapses again
description: Cuba was plunged into its seventh massive blackout of the year on Friday. The island of over nine million people endures constant power cuts due to the poor state of its aging thermoelectric plants – but the situation has worsened significantly since January, when Washington imposed a de facto energy blockade on the island. Story by Shirli Sitbon.

title: Saudi Arabia says air defences intercepted Houthi ballistic missile targeting Riyadh
description: Saudi Arabia on Saturday confirmed that Yemen’s Houthi rebels tried to attack its capital with a ballistic missile, the first targeting of Riyadh since the escalation in fighting with the rebels. The confirmation came hours after the Houthis said they targeted "sensitive sites" in Saudi Arabia.

title: Men deported from US bound and beaten in Equatorial Guinea detention hotel, lawyers say
description: <p>Group trapped at Hotel Bamy after US removal as rights groups sound alarm over poor conditions and violence</p><p></p><p>Two men that the Trump administration expelled to Equatorial Guinea were bound, fitted with bags over their heads, beaten and pushed down a flight of stairs, all in plain view of other US deportees, according to witnesses and human rights lawyers.</p><p>The men – one from Egypt and one from Eritrea – were then taken to a prison. About 30 detainees from the US remain trapped at a hotel in the outskirts of the coastal city of Malabo after being deported from the US. Detainees have said they believe the men were beaten for telling the press and human rights advocates about the poor conditions and violence inside the hotel, and that they are haunted by flashbacks and terrified they will be retaliated against next.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/18/us-men-deported-hotel-equatorial-guinea">Continue reading...</a>

title: Survivors recount panic and struggle to breathe in Nigerian prison cell where 37 died
description: <p>Police fire teargas as protests break out in city of Minna after deaths of suspected illegal goldminers, many of whom were children</p><p>Survivors from a prison cell in Nigeria where 37 suspected illegal goldminers died while in the custody of a paramilitary group this week have recounted their panic and struggle for breath, as police on Friday fired teargas at people protesting against the deaths and imposed an overnight curfew in the city of Minna.</p><p>The victims – many of whom were children – were found dead on Thursday in the cells of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), which had raided suspected illegal goldmines and ⁠locked up dozens of miners in the city, the state capital of the mineral-rich state of Niger.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/18/survivor-panic-struggle-breathe-nigeria-prison-cell-died-minna">Continue reading...</a>

title: British woman who was kidnapped in Malawi rescued by police after shootout
description: <p>Four of Nurat Osman’s alleged abductors were killed during rescue after she was taken from outside her home last week</p><p>A British woman kidnapped in Malawi last week has been rescued by police after a shootout in which four of her alleged abductors were killed.</p><p>Nusrat Osman was abducted outside her home in the southern city of Blantyre on 11 September at about 12.30pm. Police had <a href="https://www.facebook.com/malawipolice/posts/pfbid02SgvBBVEhDbZA4RnTDfUFe8ethHvTrZKKS11jX9TpEykmB8RAwA27cWqntNHMw2M2l">offered a reward</a> of 30m Malawi kwacha (£12,950) for information leading to her rescue and the arrest of the perpetrators.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/18/british-woman-kidnapped-malawi-police-shootout">Continue reading...</a>

title: Louisiana firefighters find feline native to sub-Saharan Africa while responding to house fire
description: <p>The African serval, illegally enclosed in the back yard, was subdued and transferred to an animal welfare facility </p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/louisiana">Louisiana</a> firefighters responding to a small house blaze found a wildcat native to sub-Saharan Africa illegally enclosed in the back yard, prompting an animal welfare agency to seek placing the creature in an appropriate environment, according to officials.</p><p>Firefighters investigating a report of a minor fire at a home in the suburban <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/new-orleans">New Orleans</a> community of Marrero on Tuesday spotted the cat in question – an African serval – behind the residence in a chain-linked enclosure resembling a cramped baseball batting cage, a spokesperson for the local animal protection services said.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/18/louisiana-firefighters-sub-saharan-africa-feline">Continue reading...</a>

title: ‘We demand the truth’: Olga Tokarczuk and JM Coetzee lead calls for proof of life of disappeared Eritrean writers
description: <p>More than 180 writers sign letter renewing calls for information on 12 authors detained incommunicado since 2001 crackdown on free speech by Isaias Afwerki</p><p>More than 180 writers have signed a letter to Eritrean president Isaias Afwerki calling for proof of life for 12 writers arrested in 2001.</p><p>Nobel laureates Olga Tokarczuk and JM Coetzee join prominent writers including Colm Tóibín, Elif Shafak, Isabel Allende, Ben Okri, Yann Martel, Kamila Shamsie and Tsitsi Dangarembga in signing the letter organised by PEN International and dated 18 September, marking 25 years since a government crackdown on the independent press. “Within days, Eritrea’s free press and the nation’s independent voices were systematically crushed,” opens the letter.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/sep/18/olga-tokarczuk-j-m-coetzee-lead-calls-for-release-of-disappeared-eritrean-writers">Continue reading...</a>

title: Brazil’s Lula announces higher welfare payments and free weight-loss jabs ahead of election
description: <p>Critics say moves from leftwing incumbent president are electorally motivated two weeks before Brazil’s elections</p><p>Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has announced a 15% increase in the country’s main cash-transfer programme for poor families, as well as free weight-loss jabs, prompting criticism from opponents who say the moves are electorally motivated just two weeks before the presidential election.</p><p>On 4 October, the leftwing incumbent will face the far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro, who has been <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/15/brazil-supreme-court-presidential-election">gaining ground</a> in recent weeks.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/18/brazil-lula-welfare-payments-weight-loss-jabs-election">Continue reading...</a>

title: New cat species identified for first time in more than a century in Bolivia
description: <p>New species of wild feline was discovered in Bolivia’s Yungas forest that is smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat</p><p>A diminutive wild cat that inhabits Bolivia’s ⁠cloud forest has been identified as a previously unknown species, marking the first time a new living feline species has been formally named and described in more than a century.</p><p>The cat, called tilcayo by local communities, is part of a group called tiger ⁠cats found across much of South ⁠America. It was found in Bolivia’s ​lush Yungas forest, a mountainous region where forests are often covered by clouds and surrounded by high humidity, according to researchers. It measures about 18in (46cm) long and weighs about 3lb (1.4kg), making it smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/17/new-cat-species-identified-bolivia">Continue reading...</a>

title: All smiles in Strasbourg but uncertainty clouds Canada’s EU membership plan
description: <p>Although Mark Carney welcomed offer to become bloc’s first associate member, no one seems to know what that means</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/sep/17/donald-trump-eu-european-union-mark-carney-canada-associate-membership-tariffs-threats-germany-merz-latest-news-updates">Europe live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Mark Carney received a rapturous reception in the European parliament when he gave his speech on Thursday welcoming a proposal for Canada to become the EU’s first-ever associate member.</p><p>Politicians queued to shake his hand and take selfies. One described the speech as a historic moment. “Europe has extended a hand, and Canada has taken it,” said the German Green MEP Terry Reintke, who borrowed a Canadian ice hockey shirt for the occasion.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/17/smiles-strasbourg-uncertainty-canada-eu-membership-plan-mark-carney">Continue reading...</a>

title: Battle of Chile director Patricio Guzmán dies aged 85
description: <p>Passionate documentary maker  won international acclaim for unsparing but poetic films exploring the impact of the Pinochet regime in Chile </p><p>Patricio Guzmán, the film-maker who chronicled Chile’s bloody 1970s political strife and its subsequent social and political turmoil in films such as The Battle of Chile and Nostalgia for the Light, has died aged 85. <a href="https://www.emol.com/noticias/Espectaculos/2026/09/15/1211542/muere-cineasta-patricio-guzman.html">According to Chilean news outlet Emol</a>, Guzmán died on Tuesday in Paris after a cardiorespiratory arrest.</p><p>Guzmán’s chief preoccupation throughout his career was the carnage unleashed by Augusto Pinochet’s coup in 1973 against Salvador Allende, Chile’s elected president. <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2012/jul/20/patricio-guzman-chile-master-documentary">He later told the Guardian</a>: “I’m a film-maker who was very marked by the ways of the dictator. It has remained with me for ever. I cannot leave it behind.” However, he resisted the idea that he was an activist, political film-maker, adding: “I’m not a sociologist. Neither am I a politician. I make films that are metaphorical and poetic; I interpret reality through my own personal way of looking.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/sep/16/battle-of-chile-director-patricio-guzman-dies-aged-85">Continue reading...</a>

title: People protecting nature and land set up self-defence units amid threat of murder
description: <p>Defenders of forests and rivers killed at rate of one every three days in 2025, with 85% of deaths in Latin America</p><p>Nature and land defenders were murdered at the rate of one every three days last year, prompting many communities to set up self-defence units, according to the latest annual death toll by the independent watchdog Global Witness.</p><p>Organised crime groups or professional killers were implicated in more than a third of the 124 killings of defenders in 2025 as narco-trafficking activities overlapped with intrusions into indigenous territories and environmental crime, such as illegal logging and wildcat gold mining.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/16/nature-land-defenders-self-defence-murder-organised-crime">Continue reading...</a>

title: Why China is pushing back on US warnings over rapid AI development
description: <p>Beijing believes slowdown calls aim to lock in US advantage, and is pursuing a different balance between safety and pace</p><p>About two years ago, education entrepreneur Boris But had what he calls a “penny-drop moment” – that, like countless others in China, his company needed to embrace AI before it was made obsolete by it.</p><p>His clients, well-off parents looking to send their children to study overseas, had begun arriving in his office reeling off information and opinions gleaned not from rival firms, but from chatbots.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/20/why-china-is-pushing-back-on-us-warnings-over-rapid-ai-development">Continue reading...</a>

title: Australian man accused of murdering Thai teenager and putting body in suitcase pleads not guilty
description: <p>Simon Peter Carman appeared in a Pattaya court on Friday charged with killing  Tunchanok Donhomla </p><p>An Australian man accused of murdering a Thai teenager and putting her body in a suitcase pleaded not guilty on Friday in a hearing in the seaside resort city of Pattaya, a court official said.</p><p>Simon Peter Carman, 45, was arrested in June after 17-year-old Tunchanok Donhomla was reported missing in Pattaya City, about 150km south-east of Bangkok. A suitcase containing her body was found shortly after.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/18/australian-man-accused-of-murdering-thai-teenager-and-putting-body-in-suitcase-pleads-not-guilty-ntwnfb">Continue reading...</a>

title: Weather tracker: Thunderstorms hit Spain as Japan braces for typhoon
description: <p>At least one person dead as stormy weather causes severe flooding in Barcelona and Valencia </p><p>Intense and slow-moving thunderstorms broke out on Wednesday afternoon across parts of eastern Spain, bringing some severe flooding and killing at least <a href="https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c9lyk27g8ln7o">one person</a>.</p><p>Storms first struck over the Castilla-La Mancha region during the afternoon before passing over Spain’s east coast, becoming very slow-moving and continuing overnight. Torrential rainfall, strong winds and large hail were reported in Valencia and Barcelona, causing widespread flooding in both cities. Weather stations west of Barcelona recorded some of the highest totals with more than 100mm (4in) of rain falling in the space of a few hours, and locally 70mm in just 30 minutes in the early hours of Thursday morning. Cars and roads were submerged, and flights were cancelled across the region.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/sep/18/weather-tracker-thunderstorms-spain-japan-typhoon">Continue reading...</a>

title: Japan raises interest rates to 31-year high to curb impact of rising prices
description: <p>Increase from 1% to 1.25% follows US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank tightening monetary policy</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/sep/18/japan-raises-interest-rates-central-bankers-fight-inflation-gb-retail-sales-rise-latest-news-updates">Business live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Japan’s central bank has increased interest rates to a fresh 31-year high as it attempts to combat global inflation linked to the war in Iran.</p><p>The Bank of Japan (BoJ) voted to raise its target interest rate from 1% to 1.25%, the highest level since 1995.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/sep/18/japan-raises-interest-rates-to-31-year-high-rising-prices">Continue reading...</a>

title: South Korea will not send military to support US war on Iran, defying Trump pressure
description: <p>Seoul resolves recent speculation over sending military to strait of Hormuz, saying ‘there won’t be deployment that would involve or enter war’</p><p>South Korea’s president, Lee Jae Myung, has said he will ⁠not deploy the military to the ⁠Middle East in a way ​that could draw the country into conflict, resisting calls from Donald Trump to support his war in Iran.</p><p>“There won’t be deployment that would involve or enter war. I can tell you that very clearly,” Lee said at a ⁠news conference on Friday. “We won’t deploy military assets in any form to that end.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/18/south-korea-will-not-send-military-to-support-us-war-on-iran-defying-trump-pressure">Continue reading...</a>

description: <p>This blog is now closed</p><ul><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">breaking news email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>The prime minister has been asked if Australia has any plans to join the EU, after the Canadian prime minister, <strong>Mark Carney</strong>, welcomed the offer of Canada becoming the EU’s first associate member.</p><p><strong>Anthony Albanese</strong> says “we’re a long way from Europe, of course”, but after it is pointed out that Canada is too, he says:</p><p>Our relations, of course, are also in areas that Canada doesn’t have. Our priority when it comes to Europe and our engagement with the EU is, of course, Australia-EU free trade agreement.</p><p>It was never going to be perfect, but in the legislation that we passed just in the last sitting fortnight, I can tell you … that already the eSafety Commissioner has used that strengthening of the laws to require some of the social media organisations to provide information to it, so they’ve already been compelled.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/live/2026/sep/20/australia-news-live-labor-coalition-fuel-petrol-prices-anthony-albanese-pauline-hanson-one-nation-immigration-angus-taylor-police-ntwnfb">Continue reading...</a>

description: <p>Premier Ben Carroll says if re-elected Labor will legislate a new form of manslaughter and increase maximum penalty for rape to life imprisonment</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/live/2026/sep/20/australia-news-live-labor-coalition-fuel-petrol-prices-anthony-albanese-pauline-hanson-one-nation-immigration-angus-taylor-police-ntwnfb">Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates</a></p></li><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">breaking news email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>Rapists could face life sentences and lawyers would be prevented from asking humiliating questions of victim-survivors under a suite of Victorian Labor pre-election commitments designed to reduce violence against women.</p><p>The premier, Ben Carroll, on Sunday announced an election commitment to legislate a new form of manslaughter covering cases in which a person takes their own life as a result of family violence, as well as a new offence covering perpetrators abandoning a victim in need of medical care.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/sep/20/victorian-labor-promises-new-offences-to-close-domestic-and-family-violence-loopholes-ntwnfb">Continue reading...</a>

title: Hundreds of drones target Moscow on last day of voting in Russia’s parliamentary election
description: <p>Authorities accuse Ukraine of trying to disrupt poll and say 1,600 drones in total intercepted, while at least two people killed and oil refinery damaged</p><p>Hundreds of drones targeting Moscow and its surrounding region killed at least two people and damaged a major refinery on the final day of the country’s parliamentary elections, authorities said on Sunday.</p><p>The capital’s mayor said that more than 1,600 drones had been intercepted and shot down, 450 of which were aimed at Moscow.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/20/hundreds-of-drones-target-moscow-on-last-day-of-voting-in-russias-parliamentary-election">Continue reading...</a>

title: Future of German chancellor hangs in the balance as two states go to polls
description: <p>Embattled Friedrich Merz faces nervous wait while far-right Alternative für Deutschland party targets further gains</p><p>Voters in two German states are going to the polls with the political future of the embattled chancellor, Friedrich Merz, hanging in the balance and an emboldened far right targeting further gains.</p><p>Coming two weeks after a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/12/friedrich-merz-far-right-firewall-afd-germany-future">seismic election in Saxony-Anhalt</a> in which the anti-immigration, pro-Kremlin <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/alternative-fur-deutschland-afd">Alternative für Deutschland</a> (AfD) scored its highest ever result in a regional poll, the nativist party is expected to drain support again from Merz’s conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU).</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/20/german-chancellor-friedrich-merz-state-elections-berlin-far-right">Continue reading...</a>

title: Dutch riot police break up violent far-right protest in The Hague
description: <p>Authorities ban anti-immigration march after fireworks and other projectiles thrown at officers in city centre park</p><p>Dutch riot police dispersed several hundred <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/far-right">far-right</a> protesters in The Hague on Saturday after violence erupted and local authorities banned a planned march in the city against immigration and asylum policies.</p><p>The Dutch public broadcaster NOS reported that 24 people had been arrested, after some protesters threw fireworks and other projectiles at police.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/19/far-right-protest-hague-violence-riot-police-malieveld">Continue reading...</a>

title: Jewish heirs of Holocaust victims sue California museum over Nazi-looted art
description: <p>Pasadena’s Norton Simon Museum holds 16th-century paintings stolen by the Nazis during the second world war</p><p>Jewish heirs of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/holocaust">Holocaust</a> victims and their representatives have filed two lawsuits in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/california">California</a> staking their claims to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/nazism">Nazi</a>-looted paintings that still hang on the walls of prominent museums in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/los-angeles">Los Angeles</a> and Auschwitz.</p><p>This pair of lawsuits are the first to be filed after the recent passage of laws by California and the US Congress, which strengthen US-based claims to artwork that were forcibly taken from Jewish families during the second world war.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/19/lawsuit-california-museum-nazi-looted-art">Continue reading...</a>

title: Record fuel prices across EU prompt calls for bloc-wide windfall tax on firms
description: <p>German minister says companies are ‘exploiting situation’ in Middle East, as sky-high prices become major domestic issue for leaders</p><p>European governments have discussed imposing a bloc-wide windfall tax on energy companies, as near-record fuel and gas prices pile pressure on leaders desperate to contain mounting public discontent and the challenge of the far right.</p><p>With elections due next year in eight EU countries including France, Italy, Spain and Poland, leaders are scrambling to head off the potential fallout from what analysts have warned could be one of the continent’s biggest energy shocks in decades.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/18/eu-europe-fuel-prices-calls-windfall-tax-energy-firms">Continue reading...</a>

title: Thick smoke seen near Riyadh airport as Houthis claim attack on Saudi capital
description: <p>Authorities issued warnings for city in first such alerts for Riyadh since fighting with Iran-backed Houthis escalated in July</p><p>Yemen’s Houthis said they attacked “sensitive” sites in the Saudi capital with missiles and drones, hours after flames and a large plume of black smoke were seen rising above Riyadh airport on Saturday.</p><p>The Saudi government sent air raid alerts to citizens by phone overnight warning of aerial attacks, marking the first time the government has issued such alerts for Riyadh since fighting with the Iran-backed Houthis escalated in July.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/19/saudi-arabia-riyadh-airport">Continue reading...</a>

title: Israeli president pardons combat medic who shot dead wounded Palestinian attacker
description: <p>Elor Azaria’s conviction in 2017 for manslaughter of man who stabbed soldier continues to divide country</p><p>Israel’s president has pardoned a combat medic who shot dead a badly wounded Palestinian attacker who had stabbed a soldier in the occupied West Bank, in a case that <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/jan/04/elor-azaria-israeli-soldier-exposed-faultlines">divided the country</a> a decade ago.</p><p>Elor Azaria’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/feb/21/elor-azaria-israeli-soldier-jailed-18-months-killing-palestinian">conviction in 2017 for manslaughter</a> and his release after serving two-thirds of his 18-month sentence drew enormous attention in Israel, where military service is compulsory for most Jewish men.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/19/israel-president-pardon-elor-azaria-wounded-palestinian-attacker">Continue reading...</a>

title: From ovations in Venice to death threats in Israel: the extreme responses to NAZA documentary
description: <p>As Gaza documentary wins cinematic acclaim, its directors face vitriol in Israel amid a febrile election campaign</p><p>First there was a moment of stunned silence. Then, in the Sala Grande, the main screening hall of the Venice film festival within the Palazzo del Cinema, the audience stood almost as one and turned to applaud the film-makers for 25 minutes.</p><p>The film the audience had watched for 80 harrowing minutes was the Gaza documentary NAZA, which has been produced by the Guardian.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/sep/19/ovations-venice-death-threats-israel-extreme-responses-to-naza-documentary">Continue reading...</a>

title: Yemen’s anti-Houthi forces launch inquest into sudden military collapse
description: <p>Rout raises questions about coordination and morale as some politicians claim billions of dollars were offered to persuade forces to abandon position</p><p>A bitter inquest is under way among Yemen’s anti-Houthi forces as to how what was being billed as a decisive assault on Sana’a, the Houthi-controlled capital, suddenly collapsed into a military rout.</p><p>More than 15 brigades were defeated as the country’s entire west coast fell into Houthi hands. Efforts are now being made to reorganise the anti-Houthi forces representing the UN-recognised Yemeni government in order to capture the Kahbob mountains, a strategic point from which to restrict Houthi forces moving closer to the crucial Bab al-Mandab strait.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/18/yemen-anti-houthi-forces-inquest-military-collapse">Continue reading...</a>

title: Poorest countries hit hardest by UK aid cuts under Keir Starmer government, new figures reveal
description: <p>Aid to lower-income countries fell by almost 7%, while higher-income countries saw their share of Britain’s aid budget increase</p><p>The world’s poorest countries were worst hit by British aid cuts under Keir Starmer’s government, while higher-income countries saw their share of aid increase, <a href="https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6aaabf8b0420ac660805f92a/Statistics_on_International_Development_Final_UK_ODA_Spend_2025.pdf">new figures reveal.</a></p><p>The latest figures released by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office show a 6.7% decrease in funding to the least-developed countries and low-income countries, amounting to cuts of £118m.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/sep/18/poorest-countries-hit-hardest-by-uk-aid-cuts-under-keir-starmer-government-new-figures-reveal">Continue reading...</a>

title: British Sikh man granted bail in India nine years after arrest
description: <p>Jagtar Singh Johal, from Scotland, was arrested after wedding in Punjab on alleged terrorism offences</p><p>Jagtar Singh Johal, a British Sikh man who was arrested in India in 2017 in connection with alleged terrorism offences, has been granted bail by a Delhi court.</p><p>Johal, from Scotland, was arrested for his alleged role in funding the Khalistan Liberation Force, which had carried out targeted killings in India’s Punjab region.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/sep/18/british-sikh-man-granted-bail-in-india-nine-years-after-arrest">Continue reading...</a>

title: IS member sentenced to 20 years in prison for role in 2021 Kabul airport bombing
description: <p>Mohammad Sharifullah, 28, was convicted of aiding the terrorist group that took credit for the suicide bombing </p><p>An Islamic State group member was sentenced on Wednesday to 20 years in prison for aiding the terrorist organization that took credit for a suicide bombing that killed 13 US service members and about 160 Afghans at the Kabul airport five years ago during the US military’s chaotic withdrawal from the country.</p><p>A federal jury in Virginia had convicted Mohammad Sharifullah in April of providing material support to the IS affiliate known as Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP). But jurors could not agree whether he bore some responsibility for the airport bombing on 26 August 2021.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/17/is-member-sentenced-kabul-airport-bombing">Continue reading...</a>

title: Climate crisis probably weakened glacier that caused devastating Nepal-Tibet floods, first study finds
description: <p>Scientists say global heating was a destabilising factor in collapse of 200,000 sq metre glacier in August</p><p>Climate breakdown probably weakened the glacier that collapsed causing catastrophic floods and killing over a thousand people in Nepal and Tibet last month, the first scientific study of the disaster has found.</p><p>Researchers identified unusually warm conditions before <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/27/what-caused-the-catastrophic-flash-flood-in-nepal-and-tibet-and-how-does-a-glacier-collapse">the glacier’s collapse</a>, which sent an avalanche of 110m cubic metres (3.885bn cu ft) of snow and ice into the valley below. This triggered flash floods on an almost unprecedented scale, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/02/after-the-flood-human-suffering-nepal-worst-hit-districts">hitting communities downstream</a> without warning.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/science/2026/sep/17/climate-crisis-likely-behind-deadly-nepal-tibet-floods">Continue reading...</a>

title: Imran Khan’s sons accuse Pakistani army chief of vendetta against imprisoned father
description: <p>Kasim and Sulaiman Khan tell Guardian they believe ex-PM is being ‘slowly killed’ by harsh treatment, driven by Asim Munir</p><p>The sons of Imran Khan have accused Pakistan’s powerful army chief of a “personal vendetta” against the incarcerated former prime minister and expressed fears their father is being “slowly killed” in jail, as international pressure mounts over his prison conditions.</p><p>Kasim Khan, 27, and Sulaiman Khan, 29, have become strong advocates for the release of their father, who has been held in Adiala prison in Rawalpindi since his arrest in 2023, and is serving a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/jan/17/pakistan-imran-khan-sentenced-prison-corruption-case">14-year sentence on corruption charges</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/15/imran-khan-sons-accuse-pakistan-army-chief-vendetta-asim-munir">Continue reading...</a>

title: What would it take to make India’s cities better – and safer?
description: <p>After a five-storey building collapsed in Delhi, focus is on how urban areas can adapt to growing populations. title: UK minister warns of impact of Trump’s Iran war on next month’s budget
description: <p>Bridget Phillipson says Burnham’s past criticisms of US president not an issue as PM prepares to meet Trump at UN</p><p>Next month’s budget will be made more difficult by Donald Trump’s war with Iran, one of Andy Burnham’s cabinet ministers has said, while adding she did not expect the prime minister’s previous disparaging comments about the US president to be an issue.</p><p>Burnham is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/sep/16/andy-burnham-donald-trump-un-general-assembly">expected to meet Trump</a> early next week at the UN general assembly summit in New York, the pair having previously spoken twice by phone since Burnham entered No 10.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/sep/20/uk-budget-made-harder-donald-trump-war-iran-bridget-phillipson-andy-burnham">Continue reading...</a>

title: Victims say Home Office attempt to curtail spycops inquiry will result in a ‘cover-up’
description: <p>Shabana Mahmood is concerned about length and £144m cost of inquiry into intrusive police surveillance</p><p>Victims of intrusive police surveillance have accused the government of seeking to cut short the spycops public inquiry that has been examining widespread misconduct committed by undercover officers.</p><p>The independent judge-led inquiry is scrutinising how officers, who spied on tens of thousands of political activists over more than four decades, carried out abuses such as <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2025/mar/02/revealed-at-least-25-uk-spy-cops-sexual-relations-deceived-women">deceiving women into sexual relationships</a> and <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2024/dec/03/spy-cops-officer-behaved-recklessly-by-fathering-son-while-undercover-inquiry-told">fathering children.</a></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/sep/20/victims-say-home-office-attempt-to-curtail-spycops-inquiry-will-result-in-a-cover-up">Continue reading...</a>

title: Earl Spencer says media treatment of Harry and Meghan ‘echoes’ Diana’s experience
description: <p>Comments come after he accused King Charles of gaslighting him in response to claims made in new memoir</p><p>Earl Spencer has said the relationship between the press and the Duke and Duchess of Sussex “echoes” the way the media treated his sister Diana, Princess of Wales.</p><p>In an <a href="https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cwj3d7zrgvk1o">interview with the BBC</a> to be aired on Sunday evening, Spencer described the press’s coverage of Harry and Meghan as having a “cancerous influence”, adding it would be “beholden on people to learn from Diana’s example”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/sep/20/earl-spencer-media-treatment-harry-and-meghan-echoes-diana">Continue reading...</a>

title: Thousands of pregnant women in England are reporting domestic abuse. Midwives are struggling to cope
description: <p>Exclusive: Analysis ‘lays bare’ something midwives already know from their day-to-day work</p><p>About 20,000 disclosures of domestic abuse are estimated to be made to maternity services in England every year, analysis has found.</p><p>The figures are likely to be an underestimate of the true scale of disclosures, according to experts, highlighting the role maternity professionals play in identifying abuse.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/sep/20/thousands-of-pregnant-women-in-england-are-reporting-domestic-abuse-midwives-are-struggling-to-cope">Continue reading...</a>

title: Farage says he wants to ‘hijack’ Trump’s ICE czar to help secure UK border
description: <p>Reform leader also tells US event Europe should have ‘more sensible view’ of president’s administration</p><p>Nigel Farage has said he wants to “hijack” Donald Trump’s hardline ICE adviser and bring him to the UK “to secure our borders”.</p><p>Speaking at an event in the US, the Reform UK leader also called for Europe to take a “more sensible view” of the US president’s administration rather than seeing it as “villainous”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/sep/20/farage-says-he-wants-to-hijack-trumps-ice-czar-to-help-secure-uk-border">Continue reading...</a>

title: Leftists make waves and Trump flexes muscles: US primary season takeaways
description: <p>Candidates have been selected for November’s midterms – have Republicans and Democrats made the right choices?</p><p>Primary season has official concluded in the United States, with Democrats <a href="https://www.realclearpolling.com/polls/state-of-the-union/generic-congressional-vote">leading </a>the polls among voters amid widespread economic anxieties, a war with Iran and Donald Trump’s mass deportation agenda continuing into the end of the year.</p><p>Democratic and Republican voters have selected contenders for key races in the 3 November midterms that will decide the balance of power in Congress, and the future of both parties. Democrats have been rocked by the primary victories of leftwing candidates. Republicans have doubled down on backing the president’s policies, despite his low approval ratings. And both parties are navigating the fallout from a series of scandals that have forced some candidates from the race, while others decided to press on.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/20/us-primary-season-takeaways">Continue reading...</a>

title: As White House shields the AI gold rush, Trump family and other allies strike it rich – with few guardrails
description: <p>It’s not clear that financial interests are driving White House policy, but they run parallel even as resistance mounts</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump">Donald Trump</a>’s sons, through a series of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/artificialintelligenceai">AI</a>-linked defense and technology ventures, have picked up a $620m Pentagon loan, a Marine Corps robotics contract and an undisclosed air force drone deal in the past year. His longtime friend Michael Dell won a Pentagon contract worth nearly $9bn. And this week, as public support for artificial intelligence sinks to some of the lowest levels ever recorded, the president went to bat for the industry. .</p><p>“The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades,” he posted on Truth Social Monday. “There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers.” It was the first of many aggressively pro-AI posts he would make this week.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/20/trump-ai-policy-financial-interest">Continue reading...</a>

title: Gavin Newsom signs election security bills to thwart federal interference by Trump
description: <p>Bills signed by California governor safeguard vote by mail and make seizing ballots or election records a felony</p><p>California governor Gavin Newsom has signed off on a package of bills aimed at bolstering election security, including measures to thwart federal political interference, his office announced on Sunday.</p><p>The pieces of legislation appear to address hot button national and state electoral issues, including an extension to the hours for mail-in voting drop off locations.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/19/gavin-newsom-elections-trump-administration-interference">Continue reading...</a>

title: Baby born via surrogate can leave Texas for treatment in California, court rules
description: <p>Ruling latest step in legal fight over medically fragile child born after surrogate rejected couple’s request for abortion</p><p>The Texas supreme court has decided that the month-old infant that surrogate McKenna West gave birth to can be relocated to Los Angeles, a Thursday ruling that came weeks after a California court had recognized the biological parents’ custody rights.</p><p>“Sustaining the life of the medically fragile child is the paramount concern in this time-sensitive matter,” the court <a href="https://www.txcourts.gov/supreme/orders-opinions/2026/september/september-17-2026/">wrote</a> in a Thursday order, referring to the baby’s rare severe heart defect. West had attempted to block the biological parents from removing the child from Texas and taking him to a hospital in Los Angeles where the couple live.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/19/texas-california-surrogate-court">Continue reading...</a>

title: Trump to create ‘AI Force’ to monitor technology as fears over out-of-control agents grow
description: <p>President had brushed away suggestions to slow down AI technology, even as his own party counseled caution</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump">Donald Trump</a> on Saturday said he would appoint an <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/artificialintelligenceai">artificial intelligence</a> czar and create an “AI Force” to help monitor the technology, though he gave almost no details about either plan.</p><p>As global fears over AI have grown, especially in the past week in the face of multiple industry figures sounding the alarm about its dangers, the president has been critical of calls to slow down development of the fast-moving industry.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/19/donald-trump-ai-force">Continue reading...</a>

description: The 134-km canal links southwestern China directly to the Beibu Gulf and the South China Sea, cutting cargo routes by 560 km and saving $0.77 billion a year in transport costs.

title: Russia Has No Plans to Attack Europe, But War Will Be Short if Europe Attacks Russia - Lavrov
description: YEKATERINBURG (Sputnik) - Russia does not intend to attack Europe, but if Europe attacks Russia, the war will be short, as Russian President Vladimir Putin warned, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said on Wednesday.

title: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Says No Dialogue With US on Strategic Stability
description: MOSCOW (Sputnik) - There is currently no dialogue between Russia and the United States on strategic stability, and its resumption depends on whether the US recognizes the need to improve relations with Russia, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov said on Wednesday.

title: Russian Corvette Fires Signal Flares Due to Approach of Danish Military Chopper
description: MOSCOW (Sputnik) - Russian corvette Soobrazitelny has fired two signal flares due to the approach of a Danish Air Force helicopter in the Baltic Sea to avoid provocation, the Russian Defense Ministry said on Wednesday.

title: US to Provide Ukraine Training on Software Used for Target and Route Analysis
description: WASHINGTON (Sputnik) - The US National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency has initiated a sole-source procurement to deliver commercial geospatial software training to Ukraine, according to a Sputnik correspondent’s analysis of public records on the official US federal contracting portal SAM.gov and technical documentation published by the developer.

title: SCO Calls for Binding Global Deal to Prevent Arms Race in Space
description: BEIJING (Sputnik) - The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) advocates for a legally binding international document to prevent an arms race in space and supports the safe and responsible use of artificial intelligence, SCO Secretary-General Nurlan Yermekbayev said on Wednesday.

title: Rosoboronexport Implementing Over 20 Joint Weapons Projects in Africa - CEO
description: MOSCOW (Sputnik) - Russian defense exports agency Rosoboronexport is implementing and preparing to launch over 20 projects in Africa involving the maintenance and repair of arms and military hardware, as well as the localization of their production, the company's CEO and Deputy Chairman of the Russian Engineering Union Alexander Mikheev said.

title: Houthis Report Saudi Fighter Jet Shot Down Over Yemen
description: DOHA (Sputnik) - Yemen's Ansar Allah movement, also known as the Houthis, said on Wednesday that its armed forces had shot down a Saudi fighter jet over Yemen with an anti-aircraft missile.

title: EU Admits 80% Dependence on China for Critical Raw Materials
description: MOSCOW (Sputnik) - The European Union relies on China for 80% of its supplies of critical raw materials, with its dependence on certain rare-earth materials reaching 90%, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Wednesday.
